name: The Five S Framework
headline: From care leaver. To care leader.
intro: Training that helps care-experienced people and leaders turn lived experience into leadership that lasts.
glance: 6 hours in person, or 2 hours live online

problem.scene: Kayla tells her story to 200 people.
problem.question: Everyone says it was powerful. Nobody asks what happens next.
without: A story told once at an event
with: A story that asks for something
A plan with a way to pay for it
problem.standards: Services want lived experience in the room, and care-experienced people want to lead. Leadership needs more than a story: skills, a strategy, a way to grow and someone ready to take over.
problem.evidence: Nobody has to share their own story. Storytelling in the Five S is about the story of the work, and people share only what they choose.

groups: Adults with care experience who lead, or want to lead, work in the sector
People who want lived experience leadership in their service, not just consultation

The people who support care-experienced people into leadership roles
notes: Bring a piece of work to grow

outcomes: Tell the story of your work
Tell the story behind your work so funders and partners understand why it matters, sharing only what you choose.
Name the leadership skills you have, the ones the work needs, and who could fill the gaps.
Turn an idea into a plan
Plan who the work is for, how it reaches them and how it is paid for.
Decide whether to grow the work or keep it running well where it is, and what each route needs.
Plan for the work to carry on without depending on one person, including you.
Describe how your service will support care-experienced people to lead, not only to share their story.

pillars.title: The Five S Framework
pillars.stance: From care leaver to care leader
pillars.stance_line: Five stages, in order, that take lived experience work from a story to something that lasts.
items: Choose what you share, and what you are asking people to do.
The skills you have, the ones the work needs, and who could bring them.
Who it is for, how it reaches them, and how it is paid for.
Grow the work, or keep it running well where it is.
Write down how the work runs and grow the next leaders.
pillars.base: Built on Marshall Ganz's public narrative and Moore, Riddell and Vocisano's work on how social innovations grow. The Fellowship follows the Five S over 12 months.

story_line: Five stories run through the day: Kayla, 24, Marcus, 27, Priya, 21, Jordan, 30, and Ellie, 26. Each is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.
The Care Leaders Fellowship, which he co-leads, uses the Five S Framework as its curriculum over 12 months.
He founded the Care Leavers National Movement and led the national engagement on England's new fostering standards for the Department for Education.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
proof: months: the Fellowship takes leaders through all Five S stages
Fellows led sessions at The Care Leaders Summit in York
facilitator.for_course: On the face to face day Luke leads every part. Online, he gives the keynote and answers your questions live.
